question.prompt: Let \(P\) be the parabola with equation \(y = x^2\) and let \(Q = (20, 14).\) There are real numbers \(r\) and \(s\) such that the line through \(Q\) with slope \(m\) does not intersect \(P\) if and only if \(r \lt m \lt s.\) What is \(r + s?\)

solutions.explanation:
A common point of the line and parabola must satisfy both equations, so substitute the line equation into \(y=x^2\). The line through \(Q=(20,14)\) with real slope \(m\) is
\[
y=m(x-20)+14.
\]
Thus intersection points correspond exactly to real solutions of
\[
x^2-mx+20m-14=0.
\]
The coefficient of \(x^2\) is always \(1\), so this is a quadratic for every real \(m\). It has no real solution exactly when its discriminant is negative:
\[
(-m)^2-4(20m-14)<0,
\]
or
\[
m^2-80m+56<0.
\]
This quadratic in \(m\) has two distinct real roots because \(80^2-4\cdot56>0\). Its leading coefficient is positive, so it is negative precisely between those roots. They are therefore the endpoints \(r\) and \(s\) from the question. At either endpoint the intersection equation has a real double root, so the endpoints are correctly excluded.

To find their sum without computing each root, expand the factorization:
\[
(m-r)(m-s)=m^2-(r+s)m+rs.
\]
Comparing the coefficient of \(m\) with \(m^2-80m+56\) gives \(r+s=\boxed{80}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Test the intersection equation

solutions.explanation:
For a fixed slope, compare the parabola's height with the line's height at the same horizontal coordinate. The line through \((20,14)\) is \(y=m(x-20)+14\), so define their vertical difference by
\[
F_m(x)=x^2-mx+20m-14.
\]
The graphs intersect exactly when \(F_m(x)=0\) for some real \(x\). Completing the square gives
\[
F_m(x)=\left(x-\frac m2\right)^2+C,
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
C&=20m-14-\frac{m^2}{4}\\
&=386-\frac{(m-40)^2}{4}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The squared term takes every nonnegative value, so the minimum difference is \(C\), attained at \(x=m/2\). If \(C>0\), the difference never vanishes. If \(C=0\), it vanishes at the minimum. If \(C<0\), it vanishes when \(x=m/2\pm\sqrt{-C}\). Thus nonintersection holds exactly when
\[
386-\frac{(m-40)^2}{4}>0,
\]
equivalently,
\[
40-\sqrt{1544}<m<40+\sqrt{1544}.
\]
The endpoints are symmetric about \(40\), so
\[
r+s=(40-\sqrt{1544})+(40+\sqrt{1544})
=\boxed{80},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Find the minimum vertical difference
